title: Best video tutorial software in 2026: 8 tools compared
summary: Eight video tutorial tools compared on what happens after recording: AI voiceover, written guides, translation, and the real cost of updating a tutorial.
body_markdown:
Making one tutorial video isn't the hard part. Making the hundredth one is, along with going back to fix the 99 that came before it.


On a call in September, the one person who runs both documentation and video at a B2B software company told us roughly 350 of their tutorial videos were out of date. No features had changed. The product had been visually redesigned, and an update to one main screen alone left about 100 videos needing a redo. Each five-minute video takes them about two to three hours in Camtasia: write the script, narrate it, record the screen against the narration, sync it, then add annotations and captions. They called the backlog "an eight month project for me at least."


That's the test we applied in this guide. All eight tools below can record a screen, so we compared what each one does after the recording, what it costs to change one step later, and whether you also get a written guide out of it.


## What is video tutorial software?


Video tutorial software is any tool a team uses to make a video that shows someone how to finish a task, usually in a piece of software. At minimum it records the screen. The better tools also write the narration, add the voiceover and zooms, produce a written version of the same steps, and let you fix one step later without re-recording the whole thing.


Most of what separates these tools happens after the recording. They differ in how much of the edit they do for you, whether you get a written guide alongside the video, and what a change to one step costs when the product moves next month.


## What to look for in video tutorial software


**What an update costs.** Ask a vendor what happens when step four of a published tutorial changes. If the answer is "re-record and re-edit," a library of 50 tutorials turns into a standing maintenance job within a few releases. The tools worth paying for keep the narration as editable text and let you replace one clip, so a renamed button costs minutes rather than an afternoon.


**How intuitive is the tool.** A tool that needs someone who knows video editing puts every tutorial in that person's queue. If the people who know the product best are a product manager and two support leads, check whether they can record a flow, talk through it roughly, and get a finished tutorial back without handing it to an editor.


**Whether you get the written guide too.** Plenty of readers skim a step-by-step article before they'll press play, and a support agent would rather paste an article link into a ticket than a timestamp. A tool that writes the article from the same source saves you writing it twice, and the two versions don't drift apart.


**How it sounds, in every language you need.** Subject-matter experts will record a workflow, but few of them want to record a voiceover. Check whether the tool can clean up or replace their voice, and whether translation covers the voiceover, the captions, and the written guide together at the tier you're actually buying.


## Editorial methodology and disclosure


Clueso publishes this guide and sells one of the tools in it. We rank Clueso first for one job: tutorial libraries that several people contribute to and that have to keep up with a product that changes often. Every entry, Clueso's included, says where the tool isn't the answer, and the "Is Clueso right for you?" section near the end says who should pick something else.


A tool made the list if it held a G2 rating of 4.0 or higher from at least 50 reviews and had shipped product updates in the past six months. We read each vendor's own pricing page on November 3, 2026, and each G2 rating on October 21, 2026. Feature descriptions come from vendors' own sites and pricing pages.


## The 8 best video tutorial software tools


### 1. Clueso — best for tutorial libraries that have to stay current, from any source


**What is Clueso?** Clueso is an agentic video platform for businesses. You start from a screen recording, an uploaded video, a prompt, or a slide deck or PDF, and Clueso builds a branded tutorial with an AI voiceover, zooms, captions, and motion graphics. It writes a step-by-step help article with screenshots from the same project.


**Key features**


- Start from a[screen recording](https://www.clueso.io/features/screen-recorder) in the Chrome extension or desktop recorder, an uploaded video, a chat prompt, or a[slide deck or PDF](https://www.clueso.io/features/ppt-video) , on every plan
- [AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) with 500+ voices on Free and 10,000+ on paid plans, plus an AI script rewrite that strips out filler words
- A[step-by-step help article](https://www.clueso.io/features/help-articles) written from the same recording, with screenshots at each step, exportable as Markdown, HTML, DOCX, or PDF
- Narration you edit as text, clip by clip, then regenerate, alongside a multi-track timeline, keyframes, and version history
- [AI motion graphics](https://www.clueso.io/features/motion-graphics) for steps that are clearer illustrated than recorded
- [Translation into 150+ languages](https://www.clueso.io/features/auto-translate) covering the script, voiceover, and article together; the translation glossary is Enterprise-only
- [Clueprints](https://www.clueso.io/clueprints) , reusable templates that carry layout, branding, and editing style, including a[product tutorial Clueprint](https://www.clueso.io/clueprints/product-tutorial-customer-education) (community Clueprints on every plan, custom ones on Enterprise)
- On Enterprise:[Clueso Agents](https://www.clueso.io/features/clueso-agents) that edit an existing video from an instruction,[Auto Updates](https://www.clueso.io/features/auto-updates) as a paid add-on, and quizzes, in-video interactivity, and[SCORM export](https://www.clueso.io/features/scorm-export)


**Pricing.** Free is $0 for one user with 10 minutes of video export a month. Solo is $40/month billed yearly ($50 monthly) for one user. Business is $120/month billed yearly ($150 monthly) for two users, plus $40/month per extra user billed yearly. Enterprise is custom.


**Why teams use it.** Teams pick Clueso when tutorials are a standing job, such as a help-center library or a set of videos for every release. The person who knows the workflow records it and talks through it roughly, and Clueso handles the script, voiceover, zooms, and article. Intellum's education team was on Camtasia at six to seven hours per video before switching, and produced 100+ videos for a certification course and its knowledge base in three months with Clueso ([Intellum case study](https://www.clueso.io/customers/intellum) ).


**Where it isn't the answer.** Self-serve plans meter export time: three hours a year on Solo and six on Business for two users, so a team publishing long tutorials every week will outgrow them. The features that make updates cheapest at scale, editing with AI chat through Clueso Agents and Auto Updates, are Enterprise-only.


**G2 rating.**[4.8/5 (Based on 136 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/clueso/reviews) *(Q4 2026)*


**Real review.** "It's letting us build a full tutorial video library (dozens of videos, in two languages) without needing a separate video editor or voiceover artist." —[Biz Dev, Small-Business (50 or fewer emp.), August 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/clueso/reviews/clueso-review-13336574)


> **Bottom line:** The strongest fit when tutorials are customer-facing, several people make them, and the product keeps changing.

### 2. Camtasia — best for hand-edited tutorials where every frame matters


**What is Camtasia?** Camtasia is TechSmith's desktop screen recorder and multitrack video editor.


**Update (November 2026):** TechSmith now bundles Snagit and Audiate into Camtasia's tiers as "Camtasia Snagit" and "Camtasia Audiate."


**Key features**


- Screen, camera, and audio recording, with a multitrack editor, cursor effects, annotations, and animations
- Quizzes and SCORM export from the Essentials tier
- AI voiceover from the Create tier
- Script translation and audio dubbing on the Pro tier


**Pricing.** Billed yearly only. Starter is $39/year (screen capture with a watermarked editor), Essentials is $179.88/year, Create is $249/year, and Pro is $599/year. Free trials are available. *(TechSmith store, November 2026)*


**Why teams use it.** When one tutorial has to be exactly right and someone on the team knows a timeline, Camtasia gives control over every cut, callout, and cursor move. Essentials is also the cheapest self-serve route on this list to quizzes and SCORM.


**Where it isn't the answer.** Output depends on the few people who know the editor. A product change means reopening the project and re-editing it by hand. That's the position the team in our opening is in, with about 100 videos to redo. AI voiceover needs Create, and translation needs the $599 Pro tier.


**G2 rating.**[4.6/5 (Based on 1,777 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/camtasia/reviews) *(Q4 2026)*


**Real review.** "I really like how Camtasia keeps screen recording and video editing in one simple workflow. As a content creator, I can record my screen, webcam, microphone, and system audio and then start editing immediately." —[Content Creator, Small-Business (50 or fewer emp.), September 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/camtasia/reviews/camtasia-review-13397298)


> **Bottom line:** The right tool for a video specialist polishing a few important tutorials, and a slow one once volume and frequent product changes arrive.


**Compare:**[Camtasia alternatives](https://www.clueso.io/compare/camtasia-alternatives) ·[Clueso vs Camtasia](https://www.clueso.io/vs/camtasia) ·[Camtasia vs Guidde](https://www.clueso.io/versus/camtasia-vs-guidde)


### 3. Guidde — best for short how-to videos captured click by click


**What is Guidde?** Guidde records a workflow through a browser extension, desktop app, or mobile app, then turns the captured steps into a narrated how-to video with a written version.


**Update (November 2026):** Guidde's pricing page now lists exporting a guide as an Agent Skill for Claude.


**Key features**


- Capture through a browser extension, desktop app, or mobile app
- Step-by-step scripts generated from the captured clicks
- A knowledge-base article from the video on every plan, with PDF and PowerPoint export from Pro
- AI text-to-voice from the Business plan; auto-translation is an Enterprise add-on


**Pricing.** A free plan with 25 videos (MP4 download needs a paid plan). Pro is $19 per creator/month billed yearly ($29 monthly). Business is $39 per creator/month billed yearly ($59 monthly), for up to five creators. Enterprise is custom. *(Guidde pricing page, November 2026)*


**Why teams use it.** Guidde builds its video from the steps it captured, which suits internal "how do I do X in this tool" tutorials where accuracy matters more than polish.


**Where it isn't the answer.** The video is a sequence of captured steps with a voiceover on top, so it hits a ceiling on anything customer-facing that needs pacing or polish. AI voiceover isn't on Pro, Business stops at five creators, and quizzes, SCORM, and translation sit on Enterprise.


**G2 rating.**[4.8/5 (Based on 97 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/guidde/reviews) *(Q4 2026)*


**Real review.** "The very easy-to-use UI allows my SMEs to create their own tutorials with minimal assistance from L&D." —[Global L&D manager, Enterprise (> 1000 emp.), August 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/guidde/reviews/guidde-review-13278229)


> **Bottom line:** A strong pick for internal how-to tutorials, with less editing control than customer-facing ones need.


**Compare:**[Guidde alternatives](https://www.clueso.io/compare/guidde-alternatives) ·[Clueso vs Guidde](https://www.clueso.io/vs/guidde) ·[Guidde vs Scribe](https://www.clueso.io/versus/guidde-vs-scribe)


### 4. Trupeer — best for one creator who needs a video and a document


**What is Trupeer?** Trupeer turns a screen recording into an AI-narrated video and a written document.


**Key features**


- Browser-extension capture or video upload
- AI voiceover on every plan, with premium voices from Scale
- A written document from each recording, exported as DOC, PDF, or Markdown from Pro
- Translation from the Scale plan (two languages), with more on Enterprise


**Pricing.** Free for 10 days with 1,000 credits and five-minute recordings. Pro is $40/month billed yearly ($49 monthly) for one seat and 2,000 credits. Scale is $199/month billed yearly ($249 monthly) for three seats and 10,000 credits. Enterprise is custom, from five seats. *(Trupeer pricing page, November 2026)*


**Why teams use it.** For one person making a handful of tutorials a month, Pro produces a voiced video and a document from each recording at a single-seat price.


**Where it isn't the answer.** Plans run on credits, so heavy months cost more than the sticker suggests. Translation starts on the $199 Scale plan and covers two languages there


**G2 rating.**[4.7/5 (Based on 69 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/trupeer/reviews) *(Q4 2026)*


> **Bottom line:** Fine for one creator on a budget. Translation and more seats start at $199 a month.


**Compare:**[Trupeer alternatives](https://www.clueso.io/compare/trupeer-alternatives) ·[Clueso vs Trupeer](https://www.clueso.io/vs/trupeer)


### 5. Descript — best for editing a recorded tutorial by editing its transcript


**What is Descript?** Descript is a video and podcast editor that transcribes your recording so you can cut the video by deleting words from the text.


**Key features**


- Text-based editing: delete a sentence from the transcript and the matching video goes with it
- Stock AI voices (limited on Free and Hobbyist, full from Creator) and voice clones from Hobbyist
- Caption translation into 61 languages and dubbing into 30, from Hobbyist
- Screen and camera recording in the same app


**Pricing.** A free plan with 60 media minutes a month and watermarked 720p export. Hobbyist is $16/month billed yearly ($24 monthly), Creator is $24 ($35), and Business is $50 ($65), all per person. Enterprise is custom. *(Descript pricing page, November 2026)*


**Why teams use it.** If you've recorded a tutorial with a few false starts, Descript is the fastest way to tidy it without learning a timeline, and translation arrives at a low tier.


**Where it isn't the answer.** Descript is a general-purpose editor, so it doesn't produce a written step-by-step guide, and it has no quizzes or SCORM. You still edit each tutorial yourself, which means every product change is another editing session.


**G2 rating.**[4.6/5 (Based on 930 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/descript/reviews) *(Q4 2026)*


> **Bottom line:** A good editor for recorded tutorials, with no written guide and no help keeping a library current.


**Compare:**[Descript alternatives](https://www.clueso.io/compare/descript-alternatives) ·[Clueso vs Descript](https://www.clueso.io/vs/descript) ·[Camtasia vs Descript](https://www.clueso.io/versus/camtasia-vs-descript)


### 6. ngram — best for prompt-built explainers and demos


**What is ngram?** ngram is an AI video generator that makes onboarding, training, demo, and explainer videos from a prompt or a screen recording, with an AI editor for changes afterwards.


**Key features**


- Videos from a written brief or an uploaded screen recording
- Changes requested in plain words, or made by hand in its editor
- AI audio on every plan (it draws on credits below Premium), with a custom voice from Premium
- Polls and quizzes on the Ultimate plan


**Pricing.** A free plan with 1,000 credits a month and one premium video a month up to 60 seconds; MP4 download needs a paid plan. Basic is $23.20/month billed yearly ($29 monthly), Premium is $47.20 ($59), and Ultimate is $239.20 ($299). Plans are per workspace and credit-based, with one user on Basic and Premium. *(ngram pricing page, November 2026)*


**Why teams use it.** For a short explainer or a feature demo where the brief matters more than the recording, ngram gets to a finished video from a description.


**Where it isn't the answer.** It doesn't write a step-by-step guide, and its pricing page lists no translation or SCORM. Basic and Premium allow one user, so a team needs the $239 Ultimate plan.


**G2 rating.**[4.5/5 (Based on 64 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/ngram/reviews) *(Q4 2026)*


> **Bottom line:** Worth a look for prompt-led explainers. A team building a tutorial library will hit the one-user limit quickly.


### 7. Loom — best for quick tutorials for colleagues


**What is Loom?** Loom, now part of Atlassian, records your screen and camera and gives you a share link the moment you stop.


**Key features**


- Instant screen and camera recording with a share link
- Transcripts in 50+ languages on every plan, in the language you recorded in
- Text-based editing and filler-word removal on Business + AI
- AI workflows that turn a recording into a doc or a message on Business + AI


**Pricing.** Starter is free, with 25 videos per person and a five-minute limit per recording. Business is $15 per user/month billed yearly ($18 monthly), and Business + AI is $20 billed yearly ($24 monthly). Enterprise is custom. *(Loom pricing page, November 2026)*


**Why teams use it.** No tool on this list gets from "let me show you" to a link faster, and many companies already have it installed.


**Where it isn't the answer.** Loom publishes what you recorded, pauses and all, unless you edit them out. That works for a colleague, but a customer sees every hesitation. It lists no AI voiceover or translation, and the free plan stops at five minutes a recording.


**G2 rating.**[4.7/5 (Based on 2,415 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/atlassian-loom/reviews) *(Q4 2026)*


> **Bottom line:** The fastest capture tool here, and a starting point rather than a finished customer-facing tutorial.


**Compare:**[Loom alternatives](https://www.clueso.io/compare/loom-alternatives) ·[Clueso vs Loom](https://www.clueso.io/vs/loom) ·[Guidde vs Loom](https://www.clueso.io/versus/guidde-vs-loom)


### 8. Scribe — best for written tutorials without video


**What is Scribe?** Scribe captures a workflow while you do it and writes a step-by-step guide with a screenshot for each action.


**Update (October 2026):** Scribe cut Pro Team to $13 per seat a month billed yearly, from $23, and now lists "Share as video" on every plan.


**Key features**


- Workflow capture that writes the guide as you work
- Screenshots of each step, with sensitive data redacted
- PDF, HTML, and Markdown export from Pro
- Translation and SAML SSO on Enterprise


**Pricing.** Basic is free. Pro Personal is $25/month billed yearly ($35 monthly). Pro Team is $13 per seat/month billed yearly ($17 monthly), with a five-seat minimum. Enterprise is custom. *(Scribe pricing page, November 2026)*


**Why teams use it.** For an internal tutorial that people will follow line by line, Scribe is the shortest route from doing the task to a shareable guide.


**Where it isn't the answer.** A screenshot can't show a drag, a transition, or anything where timing carries the meaning, and Scribe's pricing page lists no narration or AI voiceover. The five-seat minimum puts Pro Team at $65 a month billed yearly for a team.


**G2 rating.**[4.8/5 (Based on 978 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/scribe/reviews) *(Q4 2026)*


> **Bottom line:** The right answer when the tutorial is a written document for people inside the company.

## Which should you choose?


**Customer-facing tutorials that several people make, for a product that changes often:** Clueso.


**A few high-stakes tutorials, polished by someone who knows an editor:** Camtasia.


**Internal how-to videos made by subject-matter experts, captured click by click:** Guidde.


**One person who needs a video and a document from each recording, on a budget:** Trupeer.


**Recorded tutorials that need tidying, by someone who'd rather edit text than a timeline:** Descript.


**Short explainers and feature demos that start from a brief:** ngram.


**A quick answer to a colleague's question that will be watched once:** Loom.


**A written procedure that people inside the company follow step by step:** Scribe.


## Is Clueso right for you?


**Pick Clueso if:**


- Your tutorials are customer-facing and need to sound and look finished, with a voiceover nobody had to record.
- You want the video and the step-by-step article from the same source, without writing the steps twice.
- Several people make tutorials, and they need to come out consistent through shared Clueprints.
- Your product changes often enough that the cost of updating a tutorial matters more than the cost of making it.
- Your tutorials start from more than screen recordings, such as a prompt, a slide deck, or a PDF.


**Pick something else if:**


- You make a few tutorials a year and someone on the team already knows Camtasia well.
- The tutorial is a quick reply to a colleague that will be watched once (Loom).
- The deliverable is a written procedure with no narration (Scribe).
- You need quizzes and SCORM on a self-serve plan; Clueso has both on Enterprise, and Camtasia includes them from Essentials.

## FAQ


### What is the best video tutorial software?


It depends on who watches the tutorial and how often your product changes. For customer-facing tutorial libraries that have to keep up with releases, Clueso turns a recording, prompt, or deck into a voiced video with a[step-by-step article](https://www.clueso.io/features/help-articles) from the same source. Camtasia suits a video specialist hand-editing a few tutorials. Guidde suits internal how-tos, and Loom suits quick answers to colleagues.


### What is tutorial software?


Tutorial software is any tool that helps you show someone how to complete a task, as a video, a written step-by-step guide, or both. Video tutorial tools record the screen and turn it into a narrated video, while documentation tools like Scribe capture screenshots and write the steps. Clueso produces both from the same source, so the[video](https://www.clueso.io/features/screen-recorder) and the[written guide](https://www.clueso.io/features/help-articles) describe the same steps.


### Which AI tool can turn a screen recording into a polished software tutorial video?


Look for a tool that rewrites your rough narration into a script, voices it, and adds zooms and captions without you editing a timeline. Clueso does this from a[screen recording](https://www.clueso.io/features/screen-recorder) : it cleans up the script, adds an[AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) and zooms, and writes the help article. Guidde and Trupeer also turn recordings into narrated videos, with less control over the edit.


### What's the best software to create product tutorial videos with a voiceover?


Choose a tool where the voiceover is generated from editable text, so a changed step means rewriting a line rather than re-recording your voice. Clueso includes[AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) on every plan, with 10,000+ voices on paid plans and voice cloning on Enterprise. Camtasia adds AI voiceover from its $249-a-year Create tier, and Guidde from its Business plan.


### Is there free video tutorial software?


Yes. Clueso, Guidde, Descript, ngram, Loom, and Scribe all have free plans with limits: Clueso's covers 10 minutes of video export a month. Clueso's[free plan](https://www.clueso.io/pricing) includes the AI voiceover and the written guide, so you can test the full workflow before paying.


### How do I create a video tutorial?


Pick one task with one outcome, set up a clean account with realistic sample data, and record yourself doing it at normal speed while talking it through. Don't restart when you fumble a sentence. In Clueso, the rough narration becomes the script and an[AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) , zooms land where the action is, and the[written guide](https://www.clueso.io/features/help-articles) is generated alongside. Our guide on[how to make tutorial videos](https://www.clueso.io/blog/how-to-make-tutorial-videos) covers the steps in detail.


### Is there software that lets customers search through tutorial videos to find answers?


Yes, if the tutorials are published with a written version that a search can read. A help center that pairs each video with its step-by-step article lets customers find the right tutorial by searching for the words in the steps. Clueso publishes videos and their articles to a hosted help center that visitors can search, and Business plans add[viewership analytics](https://www.clueso.io/pricing) to show which tutorials get watched.


### How do Clueso and Guidde compare for creating software tutorials?


Both turn a capture into a narrated how-to video with a written version. Guidde builds the video from the clicks it captured, which suits short internal how-tos. Clueso gives you more control over the finished video, with a timeline,[motion graphics](https://www.clueso.io/features/motion-graphics) , and[Clueprints](https://www.clueso.io/clueprints) for consistent branding, and it can start from a prompt or a deck as well as a recording. AI voiceover is on every Clueso plan, while Guidde includes it from its Business plan. See[Clueso vs Guidde](https://www.clueso.io/vs/guidde) for the full comparison.


Before you buy, take one tutorial you've already published and ask each vendor on your shortlist to show you what it takes to change step four after a button is renamed. Time it. Multiply that by the number of tutorials your last release touched, and you'll know what each tool will cost you over the next year.
